correctness.rationale: The inverse Fourier transform of the symmetric frequency indicator is real; its square is nonnegative, in L1 and L2, and bandlimited to 2Q_t. The integer samples of each translate are the Fourier coefficients of its phase-multiplied transform on the unit frequency cube. Parseval therefore gives the claimed norm and inner-product identities for every real shift, not just samples; the common norm is positive. Convolution gives the product density proportional to (2-|eta|)^2 in each coordinate and covariance (2/5)I. The small-argument quadratic estimate and the uniform positive gap away from zero together control every lattice translate, including distant translates when taking the quotient infimum. For a finite set, truncation and renormalization control all quotient distances additively, hence relatively by the least nonzero pair distance. Base-s coding is injective on the support difference set: subtract two candidate differences and reduce coordinatewise modulo s, using strict bounds smaller than s. This matches all nonzero-shift correlations in both directions and preserves positivity and normalization. Splitting the distortion budget between the torus model and the truncation proves the stated finite claim; singleton sets are trivial. Finite determination of real L1 distortion then transfers the Khot–Naor obstruction. The supporting numerical script was inspected, not run; an independent direct evaluation reproduced 0.00130208333333074 approximately for the four listed shifts using the stated 20001 terms. This is a sampling check, not the proof.

value.rationale: The nonnegative unit constraint removes the signed model used in the prior embedding. Recovering the flat-torus finite metrics with arbitrarily small loss inside the smaller quotient shows that signal positivity does not remove its L1 obstruction. The constructive finite-realization statement is stronger than just a single bad example and is useful independently of the known lower bound.
